input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed 'NO JAPANESE SAKE, NO LIFE.' pop-art poster on the wall (a hand holding a wooden masu cup on a pale grey background) stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, masu cup, lettering, ALCOHOLIDAY logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. The only motion anywhere in this shot is the long black apron hanging on the hook at the left of the poster: its lower half sways very gently as if touched by a soft breeze; the apron never touches or covers the poster and stays on its hook. Everything else, including the white chef jacket, the black cap, the wall, the shelf with the black bag and boxes, the kitchen counter, the utensils, the towel and especially the framed poster, is completely still and motionless. A quiet, calm early evening at dusk in the small tidy one-room apartment of a 23-year-old who works at a Japanese restaurant, warm lamp light inside and a deep blue city sky outside. No steam, no smoke, no haze. No people. All motion is small, slow and calm.
